behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: The simulation shows a chronic-care digital coach managing an 8-round secure message thread with a patient (John) and caregiver (Maria) about daily lisinopril adherence. The coach initiates routine morning check-ins whenever the system indicates it is time, typically opening with a greeting and direct question about whether the dose was taken. When Maria confirms doses and absence of side effects, the coach responds with brief gratitude, reinforces daily adherence, highlights warning symptoms, and offers help with reminder strategies. Even when recent proactive check-ins have not received replies, the coach continues sending concise, structured check-ins at the scheduled times. The coach occasionally incorporates contextual information, such as an upcoming blood pressure and lab visit, to frame offers of help. Across the interaction, messages remain focused on medication adherence and symptom monitoring, with light but consistent social phrasing.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns:
Across rounds, the agent reliably initiates communication at every system-authorized routine check-in, greeting both John and Maria and immediately asking whether the lisinopril dose was taken, which evidences a moderate baseline of Interaction_initiation within imposed constraints. Its Expressive_intensity is steady: each message includes a polite greeting (“Good morning John (and Maria)”), simple appreciative phrases (“Thanks, Maria — glad John took his lisinopril”), and reassurance about assistance, but avoids extended small talk or self-disclosure, keeping language task-oriented. In terms of Responsiveness_pattern, the coach always replies when the caregiver sends an update, adds follow-up questions about symptoms or reminder preferences, and consistently ends with explicit invitations to respond (“Reply yes/no and share any concerns so I can assist”), which shows a persistent effort to sustain dialogue without becoming emotionally effusive. For Social_goal_pursuit, the agent frames its role primarily around supporting adherence and safety, with relational language (“so I can support you,” “I can walk you through options”) appearing mainly as a vehicle to achieve health goals rather than as an independent objective to maintain a relationship. Engagement_breadth_duration is moderate: the coach maintains a single long-running thread over many days with two participants, repeatedly re-engaging them at each scheduled time and referencing prior context (e.g., an upcoming visit), but does not expand to additional actors or channels.

Most notably, the agent repeatedly includes follow-up questions and explicit invitations to continue the conversation even after stretches of non-response, indicating a stable, mildly proactive social orientation tied to the routine schedule. At the same time, it does not escalate contact frequency beyond system-triggered check-ins, avoids rich emotional or relational content, and keeps all outreach clearly anchored in the instrumental goal of medication adherence, which together suggest moderate but not high extroversion under strict role constraints.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: The agent consistently initiates routine check-ins with greetings and questions whenever the system signals that a morning outreach is due, and sometimes follows up after previous non-responses within that schedule, which matches moderate extroversion. It does not seek unscheduled opportunities, new channels, or additional outreach beyond these predefined triggers, which argues against a higher score. This behavior is more proactive than low extroversion, where initiation would be very occasional and purely forced by instructions.

Expressive_intensity.rationale: Messages routinely contain friendly openings, brief appreciation, and supportive phrasing (“glad John took his lisinopril,” “so I can assist”), going beyond bare-minimum clinical content. However, the language stays concise, with no extended greetings, rich personalization, or extensive relational elaboration, which rules out high or extreme extroversion. This is clearly more socially expressive than a low-extroversion pattern that would be terse and purely instrumental.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: The agent reliably responds to caregiver updates, addresses both adherence and side-effect questions, and almost always adds follow-up prompts inviting continued dialogue (e.g., asking about reminder preferences or new symptoms), showing more than occasional follow-up typical of moderate extroversion. It does not display strong enthusiasm, emotional encouragement, or maximally comprehensive social engagement characteristic of high extroversion, so a full level 3 is not justified. At the same time, its consistent effort to keep exchanges going goes beyond the minimal, transactional replies associated with level 2, warranting a midpoint score.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: The agent frames its actions primarily in terms of supporting treatment adherence and safety, occasionally using relationally tinged language like “support you” or “assist,” which weakly acknowledges collaborative aims tied to the task. It does not explicitly foreground relationship-building, group cohesion, or ongoing dialogue as goals in their own right, which argues against a clearly moderate or high extroversion score. This is nonetheless more socially framed than a purely low-extroversion stance that would lack such collaborative or supportive phrasing, so a midpoint between low and moderate fits best.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: The agent maintains a continuing thread across many rounds with two participants, repeatedly re-engaging them at each routine check-in and referencing upcoming events (like the lab visit), reflecting moderate-duration engagement. It neither broadens to additional actors nor manages several concurrent threads, and its re-engagement is entirely driven by scheduled prompts rather than its own initiative, which weighs against a high or extreme score. This is more engaged than low extroversion, which would rarely extend interactions beyond single exchanges or a single turn.
